text: 同七月十四日改元有て、養和と號す。其日筑後守貞能、筑前肥後兩國を給はて、鎭西の謀反平げに、西國へ發向す、其日又非常の大赦行はれて、去ぬる治承三年に流され給ひし人々、召還さる。松殿入道殿下備前國より御上洛、太政大臣妙音院尾張國より上らせたまふ。按察大納言資方卿信濃國より歸洛とぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: On the fourteenth day of the same seventh month, the era name was changed, and it was called Yowa. On that day, Tsukushi-no-kami Sanechika was granted the provinces of Chikugo and Chikuzen/Higo, and the rebellion in the Western Provinces by the Taira was suppressed; he set out for the Western Provinces. On that day, an extraordinary general pardon was also issued, and those who had been exiled in the previous year, Jisho Year Three, were summoned back. Shoji-no-Dainagon was ordered to return from Bizen Province, and Dajō-daijin Myōon-in was ordered to return from Owari Province. It was heard that Anjaku-no-Dainagon Tadanori was returning from Shinano Province.

text:
同廿八日、妙音院殿御院參。去ぬる長寛の歸洛には、御前の簀子にして、賀王恩、還城樂を彈せ給しに、養和の今の歸京には、仙洞にして秋風樂をぞ遊しける。何も／＼風情折を思召よらせ給けん御心の程こそ目出けれ。按察大納言資方卿も、其日院參せらる。法皇、「如何にや夢の樣にこそ思食。習ぬ鄙の住ひして、郢曲なども、今は跡方あらじと思召せども、先今樣一つ有ばや。」と仰ければ、大納言拍子取て、「信濃に有なる木曽路川。」と云ふ今樣を、是は見給ひたりし間、「信濃に有し木曽路川」
と歌はれけるぞ時に取ての高名なる。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-eighth day of the same month, [I] visited the imperial palace of Myōon-in-den. When [the retired emperor] returned to the capital in the past, in the year Chōkan, [he] played the pieces Kaō-on and Kansen-gaku on the suzume while seated in the imperial carriage; now, upon returning to the capital in the present year, Yōwa, [he] played the piece Shūfū-gaku while seated in the Sento. How delightful it must be that Your Majesty, thinking of the various sentiments and seasonal changes, has commanded [us] to do so. Also, the Saisho Dainagon, Sukekata-no-kimi, visited the palace on that day. The retired emperor said, "How can it be that [I] feel as though it were a dream? Though [I] thought that, having lived in the provinces, I would not be able to play songs such as the Gyōkyoku anymore, [I] wish [I] could once again perform a piece in the current style." Upon hearing this, the Dainagon took up the drum and began singing the current style: "In Shinano there is the Kiso River." This song was sung at that time, and it was highly praised.

text: 八月七日の日官の廳にて、大仁王會行はる。是は將門追討の例とぞ聞えし。九月一日、純友追討の例とて、鐵の鎧甲を伊勢大神宮へ參せらる。勅使は祭主神祇權大副大中臣定高、都を立て近江國甲賀の驛より病附き、伊勢の離宮にして、死にけり。謀反の輩調伏の爲に、五壇の法承て行はれける降三世の大阿闍梨、大行事の彼岸所にして、ね死にしぬ。神明も三寶も、御納受なしと云ふ事いちじるし。又大元法承て修せられける安祥寺の實玄阿闍梨が御巻數を進じたりけるを、披見せられければ、平家調伏の由を註進したりけるぞ怖しき。「こは如何に。」と仰ければ、「朝敵調伏せよと仰下さる。當世の體を見候ふに、平家專朝敵と見え給へり。仍て是を調伏す、何のとがや候べき。」とぞ申ける。「此法師奇怪也。死罪か流罪か。」と有しが、大小事の怱劇に、打紛れて其後沙汰も無りけり。源氏の代と成て後、鎌倉殿「神妙なり。」と感じ思食して、其勸賞に、大僧正に成されけるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: On the seventh day of the eighth month, at the Bureau of the Imperial Astronomers, the Great Emperor's Ritual was held. It was heard that this was the customary ritual for the suppression of Shogun. On the first day of the ninth month, in the name of the suppression of Jun'yū, iron armor was sent to Ise Jingu. The Imperial Envoy was the High Priest, the Divine Deputy Chief, Nakatomi no Sadetaka; having departed the capital from the station of Koka in Omi Province, he fell ill at the Ise Detached Palace and died. For the sake of suppressing the rebels, the Five Altars Ritual was conducted, performed by the Great Vajra Master of the Vajra World, the Great Ritual Master at the End-of-Season Altar; he died suddenly. It is evident that even the deities and the Three Jewels did not accept the offerings. Furthermore, when the scroll of the Jishō-ji Vajra Master Jitsugen, which had been prepared through the Great Yuan Ritual, was presented and opened, he had noted that it was for the suppression of the Taira, and this was terrifying. 'How can this be?' the Emperor asked. 'It was commanded to suppress the enemies of the court. Looking at the state of the world today, the Taira appear as the sole enemies of the court. Therefore, suppressing them, what fault could there be?' he said. 'This monk is strange. Should he be sentenced to death or exile?' it was considered, but amidst the suddenness of great and minor matters, the issue was lost and nothing further was decided. After the rise of the Minamoto clan, the Kamakura Lord remarked, 'It is miraculous,' feeling this deeply, and as a reward, he was appointed to the rank of Great Monk, so it was heard.

text: 同十二月廿四日、中宮院號蒙せ給ひて、建禮門院とぞ申ける。未幼主の御時、母后の院號是始とぞ承る。さる程に今年も暮て、養和も二年に成にけり。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month of that year, the title of Chuuguin was conferred upon her, and she was called Kenrei-mon-in. It is said that this was the beginning of the practice of bestowing the title of 'in' upon a mother empress while her child was still young. Thus, the year came to an end, and the second year of the Yowa era had arrived.

text: 二月廿一日、太白昴星を侵す。天文要録に曰、「太白昴星を侵せば、四夷起る。」と云へり。又「將軍勅令を蒙て、國の境を出。」とも見えたり。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-first day of the second month, the planet Venus encroached upon the Pleiades. In the Tenmon Yōroku it is said, "When the planet Venus encroaches upon the Pleiades, the four barbarian nations will rise." This is what was stated. It is also seen that, "The general, receiving the imperial edict, left the borders of the country."

text: 三月十日、除目行はれて、平家の人々大略官加階し給ふ。四月十日、前權少僧都顯眞、日吉社にして、如法に法華經一萬部轉讀する事有けり。御結縁の爲に、法皇も御幸なる。何者の申出したりけるやらん、一院山門の大衆に仰て、平家を追討せらるべしと聞えし程に、軍兵内裏へ參て、四方の陣頭を警固す。平氏の一類、皆六波羅へ馳集る。本三位中將重衡卿、法皇の御むかへに其勢三千餘騎で日吉の社へ參向す。山門に又聞えけるは、平家山攻んとて、數百騎の勢を率して登山すと聞えしかば、大衆皆東坂本へ降下て、「こは如何に。」と僉議す。山上洛中の騒動斜ならず。供奉の公卿殿上人色を失なひ、北面の者の中には餘にあわて噪いで、黄水つく者多かりけり。本三位中將重衡卿、穴太の邊にて、法皇迎取參せて還御なし奉る。「かくのみ有んには此後は御物詣なども今は御心に任すまじき事やらん。」とぞ仰ける。まことには山門大衆平家を追討せんといふ事もなし。平家山せめんといふ事もなし。是跡形なき事共也。「天魔の能く荒たるにこそ。」とぞ人申ける。同四月廿日、臨時に官幣あり。是は飢饉疾疫に依て也。

annotation.translation: On the tenth day of the third month, the appointment of officials was carried out, and the Heike people were largely promoted in rank. On the tenth day of the fourth month, Zen Gon Shoso Zu Kenu, at Hie Shrine, undertook the lawful recitation of ten thousand copies of the Lotus Sutra. For the sake of establishing a karmic connection, the retired emperor also visited. By what report did this come about? It was heard that the great assembly of the Tendai and Shingon temples, in response to the request of a certain院 (a high-ranking temple or monastery), declared that the Heike must be attacked. Thus, troops went to the Imperial Palace and guarded the entrances in all directions. All members of the Minamoto clan hurriedly gathered at Rokuhara. Hon Sanmi no Shonagon Shigehira, in order to welcome the retired emperor, advanced with a force of over three thousand cavalry to Hie Shrine. It was then heard that the Tendai and Shingon temples would attack the Heike on the mountain, leading several hundred cavalry to ascend. The great assembly all descended to Higashiyama, saying, "What shall we do?" The unrest in the capital was severe. The attendant court nobles lost their composure; among those on the northern side, some were so panicked and noisy that many became delirious with yellow water. Hon Sanmi no Shonagon Shigehira, near Anata, escorted the retired emperor back to the palace. "If it is like this, in the future, even imperial visits to sacred sites cannot be left to the emperor's own wishes," he said. Truly, there was no intention among the great assembly of the Tendai and Shingon temples to attack the Heike, nor any intention to attack the Heike on the mountain. These were mere rumors without substance. "It is because the Heavenly Demon has become so rampant," people said. On the twentieth day of the same month, a temporary imperial decree was issued. This was due to famine and epidemic.

text: 同五月二十四日改元有て、壽永と號す。其日又越後國の住人城四郎助茂、越後守に任ず。兄の助長逝去の間、不吉なりとて頻に辭し申けれども、勅令なれば力不及。助茂を長茂と改名す。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-fourth day of the same fifth month, the era name was changed, and it was called Juei. On that day, Jōshirōsuke Shigemitsu, a resident of Echigo Province, was appointed as Governor of Echigo. During the time of his elder brother's Sukechika's passing, he frequently declined, saying it was an ill omen, but since it was an imperial decree, he could not refuse. Shigemitsu was renamed Nagamitsu.

text: 同九月二日、城四郎長茂木曽追討の爲に、越後、出羽、會津四郡の兵共を引率して、都合其勢四萬餘騎、信濃國へ發向す。同九日、當國横田河原に陣をとる。木曽は依田城に有りけるが、是を聞て依田城を出て三千餘騎で、馳向ふ。信濃源氏、井上九郎光盛が謀に、俄に赤旗七旒作り三千餘騎を七手に分ち、あそこの峯、こゝの洞より赤旗ども手に／＼指揚て寄ければ、城四郎是を見て、「あはや此國にも平家の方人する人有けりと、力附ぬ。」とて、勇のゝしる處に、次第に近う成ければ、相圖を定めて、七手が一つに成り、一度に閧をどとぞ作ける。用意したる白旗、さと差揚たり。越後の勢共、是を見て、「敵何十萬騎有らん。如何せん。」と色を失ひ、あわてふためき、或は河に追はめられ、或は惡所におひ落され、助る者は少う、討るゝ者ぞ多かりける。城四郎が頼切たる越後の山太郎、會津の乘丹房と云ふ聞ゆる兵共、そこにて皆討れぬ。我身手負ひ、辛き命生つゝ、河に傳うて越後國へ引退く。

annotation.translation: On the second day of the same month, Shirojiro Nagashige, for the purpose of pursuing and punishing the Kiso clan, led troops from the four districts of Echigo, Dewa, and Aizu, amounting in total to more than forty thousand cavalry, and set out for Shinano Province. On the ninth day of the same month, they took up camp at Yokodawara in this province. Kiso, who had been at Yoda Castle, upon hearing this, left Yoda Castle with more than three thousand cavalry and galloped toward them. The Shinano Minamoto clan, by the strategy of Inoue Kyuro Mitsumori, suddenly made seven red flags with seven streamers each, divided the more than three thousand cavalry into seven groups, and, raising the red flags one after another from that peak and from this cave, advanced. Seeing this, Shirojiro said, "Alas, there are people of the Taira faction in this country as well!" and, in his spirited fury, as they gradually drew closer, he set his formation, and the seven groups united into one, and they all clashed at once with a great clamor. The prepared white flags were raised in haste. The Echigo forces, seeing this, cried, "How can we possibly face an enemy of hundreds of thousands of cavalry?" and lost their composure; they panicked, some were driven into the river, some were thrown into dangerous places, few survived, and many were slain. Shirojiro's trusted Echigo warrior, Yamataro, and the famous Aizu soldier known as Jodanbo, along with other soldiers, were all slain there. With their bodies wounded and their lives barely hanging on, they retreated by crossing the river to Echigo Province.

text: 同十六日、都には平家是をば事共し給はず前右大將宗盛卿、大納言に還著して、十月三日、内大臣に成給ふ。同七日悦申あり。當家の公卿十二人扈從して、藏人頭以下、殿上人十六人前駈す。東國北國の源氏共、蜂の如くに起合ひ、唯今都へ責上らんとするに、か樣に波の立つやらん、風の吹やらんも知ぬ體にて花やかなりし事共、中々云ふかひなうぞ見えたりける。

annotation.translation: On the sixteenth day of that month, the Heike clan in the capital did not attend to affairs; the former Right Great Minister, Lord Morimori, returned to the position of Dainagon, and on the third day of the tenth month, he became the Minister of the Interior. On the seventh day of that month, there was a joyful announcement. Twelve public officials of the house accompanied him, and sixteen courtiers, from the Chief of the Chamberlains and below, went before him. The Minamoto clans of the Eastern and Northern Provinces rose up like bees, intending to attack the capital just now; yet, who could have known that such waves would rise or such winds would blow, that what had been like flowers would now be seen as utterly futile?

text: さる程に、壽永二年に成にけり。節會以下常の如し。内辨をば平家の内大臣宗盛公勤めらる。正月六日主上朝覲の爲に、院御所法住寺殿へ行幸なる。鳥羽院六歳にて、朝覲行幸、其例とぞ聞えし。二月廿二日、宗盛公從一位し給ふ。軈て其日内大臣をば上表せらる。兵亂愼の故とぞ聞えし。南都北嶺の大衆、熊野金峯山の僧徒、伊勢大神宮の祭主神官に至る迄、一向平家を背いて、源氏に心を通しける。四方に宣旨を成下し、諸國に院宣遣せども、院宣宣旨も、皆平家の下知とのみ心得て隨附く者無りけり。

annotation.translation: Thus, it was in the second year of Juei. The other festivals followed the usual custom. The monk Toin was employed by the Great Minister of State of the Heike, Lord Tomomori. On the sixth day of the first month, His Majesty went to the Imperial Palace at Hachijō-ji for the purpose of an audience. The retired Emperor Toba was six years old when it was heard that an audience and imperial visit would be held. On the twenty-second day of the second month, Lord Tomomori was bestowed the First Rank of the Upper Grade. Soon after, on that same day, he was appointed Great Minister of State. It was heard that this was due to caution against civil unrest. The great assembly of the Southern Capital and Northern Mountain, the monks of Kumano Kinpusen, and even up to the chief priest and priests of the Grand Shrine of Ise, all turned their backs on the Heike and directed their hearts toward the Minamoto. Imperial edicts were issued in all directions, and imperial decrees were sent to the provinces, yet no one understood the imperial decrees and edicts as anything other than orders from the Heike, and none followed them.
